system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Metachromatic leukodystrophy due to arylsulfatase A deficiency
mechanism: Arylsulfatase A deficiency impairs lysosomal degradation of sulfatides, causing sulfatide accumulation in the central and peripheral nervous systems with progressive demyelination and neurodegeneration.
vignette: A previously healthy young child develops progressive gait difficulty, frequent falls, loss of previously acquired language skills, and peripheral neuropathy. Brain MRI shows symmetric confluent white-matter abnormalities. Enzyme testing demonstrates markedly reduced arylsulfatase A activity.
lead: Accumulation of which of the following substances most directly causes this disorder?
distractor_notes: Galactocerebroside accumulates in Krabbe disease due to galactocerebrosidase deficiency.
Glucocerebroside accumulates in Gaucher disease due to glucocerebrosidase deficiency.
Sphingomyelin accumulates in acid sphingomyelinase deficiency, classically Niemann-Pick disease types A/B.
GM2 ganglioside accumulates in Tay-Sachs disease due to hexosaminidase A deficiency.
key_expl: Arylsulfatase A normally participates in lysosomal degradation of sulfatides. Deficient ARSA activity causes sulfatide accumulation, damaging myelin in both the central and peripheral nervous systems and producing the progressive motor, cognitive, and neuropathic manifestations of metachromatic leukodystrophy.
objective: Connect arylsulfatase A deficiency with lysosomal sulfatide accumulation in metachromatic leukodystrophy.
